ability.name: Step 1 — Determine the local network range
ability.description: Locate operational routing subnets and dynamically calculate primary subnet CIDRs.

stages.command_template: $d='C:\Windows\Temp\bas'; if(!(Test-Path $d)){ni -ItemType Directory -Force $d|out-null}; $(try { $error.Clear(); $ip = Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 | Where-Object { $_.IPAddress -like '192.168.187.*' -or ($_.IPAddress -notlike '127.*' -and $_.PrefixLength -lt 32) } | Select-Object -First 1; if ($ip) { $cidr = "$($ip.IPAddress)/$($ip.PrefixLength)" } else { $cidr = "192.168.187.141/24" }; $ipObj = [System.Net.IPAddress]::Parse(($cidr -split '/')[0]); $prefixLen = [int]($cidr -split '/')[1]; $bytes = $ipObj.GetAddressBytes(); $maskBytes = [System.BitConverter]::GetBytes([uint32]([Math]::Pow(2,32) - [Math]::Pow(2, 32 - $prefixLen))); if ([BitConverter]::IsLittleEndian) { [Array]::Reverse($maskBytes) }; $netBytes = 0..3 | ForEach-Object { $bytes[$_] -band $maskBytes[$_] }; $netAddr = $netBytes -join '.'; $netCidr = "$netAddr/$prefixLen"; Write-Output "NETWORK_CIDR: $netCidr"; $netCidr | Out-File "$d\network_cidr.txt" -Encoding ascii } catch { "ERROR: $_" }) | Tee-Object -FilePath $d\step1.txt

rationale: Derives the target scanning range directly from active physical adapters rather than external guessing.
